name: Ensure the 404 flag always produces a 404 in React/Inertia pages
description:
## Why?

PR [#44919](https://github.com/shoptet/cms4/pull/44919) () fixed a cross-tenant leak on PartnerService* pages: a legacy controller set displayPage404 = true but kept executing, so the page rendered another tenant's real data with no 404. Petr Kostka flagged that this class of bug — a 404 flag set but not enforced — needs a systemic fix, not a one-off patch, since more Smarty→React rewrites will hit the same "flag instead of exception" pattern.

## What?

When a page signals it should 404, the React/Inertia response must always be a real 404, or at minimum must never carry page data. Where possible, React itself should handle this case — e.g. a shared page wrapper treating a 404 signal/prop as a hard 404 — rather than relying on every backend call site getting the flag-vs-exception distinction right. The st-tpl-to-react rewrite skill should also document this as an explicit rule so future rewrites raise a proper exception instead of silently setting a flag.

## Acceptance criteria

A page whose backend controller sets the legacy 404 flag during an Inertia/React page build returns a real 404 response — never page props with tenant/entity data.

React's shared Inertia page handling treats a 404 signal as a hard 404 wherever feasible, instead of depending solely on each backend controller doing it right.

The st-tpl-to-react skill's guidance/checklist explicitly calls out this pattern (flag → exception) so new rewrites don't reintroduce it.

Other admin/controllers/ call sites using the same "set flag, keep executing" pattern are identified and triaged (fixed, or explicitly accepted with reason).
